coverage_note: Philadelphia independent district comparison, 2024–25: all 162 audited grade schools enter each Math, ELA and Combined model. Original regular PSSA All Students / Total rates and verified Number Scored match each school’s own October individual PIMS low-income ratio. Conditional sampling intervals use all model members and fixed deleted scales; Combined uses maximum positive subject covariance and displays the smaller subject count, not a paired count. The full source preserves 221 CCD links, 59 outside records and the separate native 9999 aggregate with no inferred CCD identity or school income. Native and CCD enrollment/income differences have unassigned causes. Keystone, PASA and charter LEAs remain separate. Admissions, provider roles, programs, coordinates and boundaries remain unaudited; one year only.

methodology.summary: Philadelphia independent regular PSSA grade-school models with individual October PIMS income, verified scored counts and approximate conditional sampling intervals.
details: Philadelphia independent 2024–25 grade-school district models use exact NCES LEA 4218990 / PA-126515001 / native AUN 126515001 identities. All 162 audited pure lower profiles with positive October grades 3–8 and explicit-zero grades 9–12 remain searchable and enter separate fixed Math, ELA and independently fitted Combined models. Original regular PSSA All Students / Total published proficiency and Number Scored are matched to each school’s own October individual PIMS low-income ratio. Conditional sampling intervals propagate every model member’s scored-count variance while holding deleted regression scale fixed. Combined uses the maximum positive Math/ELA covariance bound and displays the smaller subject count; this display is not a paired or deduplicated denominator. High, mixed, primary, inactive and unmatched records remain outside the release; Keystone and PASA remain separate.

Three separate unweighted OLS fits reproduce all 486 audited results and explicit deleted fits. Combined independently fits the equal mean of original Math and ELA rates, with its own scale and studentization. Filters never refit. Associations do not establish causal effectiveness or overall quality.

Regular PSSA includes native grades 3–8 and the published All Students / Total accountable scored population. Original notes exclude post-October 1 enrollment, homeschoolers, excluded school aggregations, ELL enrolled less than one year, LIFE pupils entering EL after the prior testing window and pupils who did not attempt. Proficiency uses the directly published Proficient and above percentage, with one-decimal rounding; rounded levels and grade rates are never summed or averaged. Keystone end-of-course and PASA alternate assessment remain separate.

October 1, 2024 school individual PIMS Economic Disadvantaged Status Code field 88: own low-income enrollment divided by own same-year total enrollment, including enrolled pre-K/kindergarten categories. TANF, census poor, Medicaid, neglected/delinquent institutions and foster homes are allowed sources; recent reliable FRPL is a fallback. CEP must use individual poverty sources rather than universal meals. Field 131 food-program eligibility is separate. The published proportion truncates to four decimals; the comparison uses the precise original count ratio. Local source choices and reporting coverage remain unknown; no LEA income allocation, another denominator or year is substituted.

Native October LEA enrollment 120,148 differs from operational school/income enrollment 116,286; CCD reports 120,057 and 116,230 respectively. Native 9999 accounts for 3,862 enrolled pupils but has no exact CCD identity or school income. Native LEA low-income 90,098 versus school 88,634 leaves 1,464 unassigned. These differences do not establish their causes or authorize income allocation. Inactive Meehan is never substituted for 9999; K–2 Barton remains outside.

Number Scored is the original same-year regular PSSA All Students / Total valid-score denominator. Published usable rates require at least 11 scored; the 324 released subject counts are all at least 42. Approximate conditional 95% intervals use Jeffreys-smoothed binomial variance from published rounded rates, all-member (I−H) propagation and a fixed deleted regression scale. Combined uses maximum positive subject covariance and displays the smaller subject count only, not a paired or deduplicated count. Enrollment, participation and federal 95%-rule counts never substitute. Studentization uses N−3 deleted degrees of freedom; it provides no enrollment adjustment or shrinkage. Intervals condition on income, design and deleted scale and approximate sampling alone; local poverty-source choice and accountable population/rounding uncertainty remain limits.

All full and 486 deleted designs have rank two and finite positive scales. Largest deleted prediction changes over observed incomes: Math 1.850114; ELA 1.926300; Combined 1.888207 percentage points. Meredith and Greenfield ELA predictions above 100% remain unclipped; Jenks Abram’s authoritative NCES/native school-number suffixes differ. Influence never removes a school.

The complete source preserves 22,108 original records and 622,260 typed cells with original headers, notes and definitions. Compact references preserve exact table, worksheet, row and field evidence. Historical audit approvals remain false; only the separately validated grade-school comparison is released.

High, mixed, primary, inactive, unmatched and separate charter-LEA records remain outside the 162 released profiles. Programs are Unclassified; admissions, provider roles, coordinates and boundaries remain unknown. One year only; incompatible thresholds and income definitions cannot form a national ranking.
